title: Bird point counts at 1,353 points over 15,182 visits, southern Sierra Nevada, California, 2009 to 2016 (coordinates coarsened)
creator: Roberts, Lance Jay; Burnett, Ryan; Tietz, James; Veloz, Sam
citation: Roberts, L. J., Burnett, R., Tietz, J., & Veloz, S. (2018). Data from: Recent drought and tree mortality effects on the avian community in southern Sierra Nevada: a glimpse of the future? [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.rm2n805
samplingProtocol: Point counts at points on 5-point transects, one or two visits a year in the breeding season; each detection recorded with count, cue and distance at first detection; y = individuals of the taxon detected at the visit, summed over its records at all distances.
closureNote: the one or two visits to a point within a breeding season are the occasions; years are periods.
covariateNote: obs_tod_h: time of day (decimal hours); obs_temp_c: temperature (deg C); obs_wind_bft: wind (Beaufort). unit_site: pair of transects. Site covariates (from the site-covariate file, 184 points, NA elsewhere): forest condition, conifer die-off from GIS and from field crews (% of standing trees within 100 m dead), CWHR forest type, elevation (and, in the exact table, its residual on latitude), aspect, slope, solar radiation index, southness, shrub and tree cover (%), basal area (ft2/acre), snags > 30 cm and > 10 cm, max DBH (inches, within 50 m), pine proportion, NDWI and its change from 2009, climatic water deficit (mm) and June min / max temperature with their changes from 2009. Each is unit_ when constant across a point's years, otherwise period_.
notes: Visits are taken from the record file, which carries an explicit row for a visit with no detection; 30 point-years of the site-covariate file have no records and are not in the table, and its MaxOfVisit differs from the record file's visit count at 119 point-years. Taxa resolved through the IBP-AOS alpha-code list; WESJ and GRAJ are superseded codes, WEFL and SAGS slash pairs. Coordinates exist for the 184 points of the site-covariate file only.
abstract: Avian point counts in the southern Sierra Nevada, California, used to model the effects of temperature, water deficit and drought-driven tree mortality on 45 bird species. Points on 5-point transects (transects paired into sites) counted once or twice a year from 2009 to 2016; every bird detected was recorded with its distance. One row per point visit x taxon, y = individuals detected (all distances). Habitat, tree-mortality and climate covariates for 184 of the points (2010-2016). Coordinates coarsened to 0.1 degree because Coccothraustes vespertinus (IUCN VU) is in the table; roberts_2019_sierrane_birds_exact_count has the other taxa at the published coordinates.
geographicCoverage: Southern Sierra Nevada, California, USA (coordinates, for 184 points, coarsened to 0.1 degree)

coordinatesCoarsened.method: point coordinates replaced by 0.1 degree cell centres (coarsen_coords) because Coccothraustes vespertinus (IUCN VU), native here, is in the table; elevation rounded to 100 m and its residual not shipped (E7.4)

notShipped.undefined_codes: 3438 records in 24 codes neither the deposit nor the IBP-AOS list defines (XX.. and X... groups such as XXWO, XXSA, XXEM, XXXX); the 3 '---' rows mark visits with no detection and become rows of zeros
notShipped.distances_cues: distance at first detection and detection cue per record (a distance-sampling table could be built)
notShipped.visit_keys: Rep2 and DOY (recoverable from period, occasion and date)
notShipped.max_of_visit: MaxOfVisit of the site-covariate file, which disagrees with the record file at 119 point-years (the record file is believed)
notShipped.future_covariates: the three future-climate covariate files (inputs to the authors' projections)
notShipped.model_output: the modelled species list's detection functions, abundance estimates and projections
notShipped.elev_residual: elevres (elevation residual, a locator with latitude; E7.4); in roberts_2019_sierrane_birds_exact_count
